flawed_step: Any proof has to go from "each vertex's neighbourhood has a Hamiltonian cycle" to "the whole graph has one." That step fails. The local condition does not even force the graph to be connected: two disjoint copies of K4 satisfy it. Even among maximal planar graphs, it does not prevent a toughness failure, where removing k vertices leaves more than k components. Such a failure rules out a Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample:
Build a triangulation T by starting with the octahedron and placing one new vertex inside each face. The octahedron has 6 vertices: north N, south S, and equator vertices u1, u2, u3, u4, with u1-u2-u3-u4-u1 a 4-cycle. It has 12 edges: N-ui, S-ui, and ui-u(i+1). Its 8 faces are N ui u(i+1) and S ui u(i+1), for i = 1..4 with indices mod 4. In each face xyz, add a vertex f joined to x, y and z.

Size of T: 14 vertices and 12 + 24 = 36 edges. Since 36 = 3·14 − 6, T is a maximal planar graph.

T is locally Hamiltonian:
(a) A face vertex f in face xyz has neighbourhood {x, y, z}. These three vertices form a triangle, so the neighbourhood has a Hamiltonian cycle.
(b) Vertex N has neighbours u1, u2, u3, u4 and the face vertices a1..a4, where ai is the vertex in face N ui u(i+1). The neighbourhood contains the cycle u1 a1 u2 a2 u3 a3 u4 a4 u1. Each edge ui–ai and ai–u(i+1) exists because ai is joined to its face's corners. S works the same way.
(c) Vertex u1 has neighbours N, u2, S, u4 and the face vertices of faces Nu1u2, Su1u2, Su4u1 and Nu4u1. The neighbourhood contains the cycle N – f(Nu1u2) – u2 – f(Su1u2) – S – f(Su4u1) – u4 – f(Nu4u1) – N. The edges N-u2, u2-S, S-u4 and u4-N are not needed. Each face vertex is joined to both cycle-neighbours listed beside it, since both are corners of its face. The other equator vertices work by symmetry.

T is not Hamiltonian: delete the 6 octahedron vertices. The 8 face vertices are pairwise non-adjacent, so what remains is 8 isolated vertices, i.e. 8 components. Deleting k vertices from a Hamiltonian cycle leaves at most k paths, so any Hamiltonian graph minus k vertices has at most k components. Here 8 > 6, so T has no Hamiltonian cycle.

(A simpler witness under the literal definitions: two disjoint copies of K4. Every neighbourhood is a triangle, and the graph is disconnected, so it is not Hamiltonian.)
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The 14-vertex triangulation made by adding a vertex inside each face of the octahedron is maximal planar and locally Hamiltonian. It is not Hamiltonian: deleting the 6 octahedron vertices leaves 8 isolated vertices, and a Hamiltonian graph minus 6 vertices can have at most 6 components. Two disjoint copies of K4 also refute the general claim.
